content.text:
The safe initialization path is a full in-place rebuild while preserving the existing Brain. Do not run `entire brain reset --force`: this repository already has a 6.1 GB Brain with roughly 6,260 distilled facts.

Current state:

- Entire is enabled; Codex and Gemini hooks are current.
- Brain `v0.1.0-416-g58b0c54e` and Graph are installed.
- `main` currently matches `origin/main`.
- Three untracked paths make the worktree dirty: `.agents/` and two files under `outputs/`.
- The old Brain manifest contains one obsolete field that the new binary rejects.

## 1. Stop writers and make the checkout clean

Stop any running `entire brain watch` process and finish active agent sessions. Then:

```sh
cd ~/Projects/entire.io

entire status --detailed
git status --short
```

Either commit the untracked files if they belong in the repository, or temporarily stash them:

```sh
git stash push --include-untracked \
  -m "pre-brain-init-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"

git fetch --prune origin
git pull --ff-only origin main
git status --short
```

The final `git status --short` should produce no output.

## 2. Reverify the installed components

```sh
entire plugin doctor
entire graph version
entire graph doctor --json
entire brain version
entire brain config show
```

Expected:

- `entire plugin doctor` says all plugins are healthy.
- Graph doctor reports `"no_egress": true`.
- Brain reports `v0.1.0-416-g58b0c54e`.

The global Brain config already exists, so do not rerun `entire brain config init` unless you intentionally want to overwrite it with defaults.

## 3. Back up the existing Brain

There is currently enough disk space for a full 6.1 GB backup.

```sh
brain_dir="$(entire brain path "$PWD")"
brain_state_dir="$HOME/.local/state/entire/repos/gh/entirehq/entire.io"
brain_stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"

brain_data_backup="${brain_dir}.pre-init-${brain_stamp}"
brain_state_backup="${brain_state_dir}.pre-init-${brain_stamp}"

test ! -e "$brain_data_backup"
test ! -e "$brain_state_backup"

cp -a "$brain_dir" "$brain_data_backup"
cp -a "$brain_state_dir" "$brain_state_backup"

du -sh "$brain_dir" "$brain_data_backup"
```

Keep these backups until the refreshed Brain has been verified.

## 4. Repair the one incompatible manifest field

The obsolete field is derived seed-coverage metadata, not a fact or session. I validated this repair against a temporary copy: removing it makes the manifest readable by the new binary.

```sh
brain_manifest_tmp="$(mktemp "$brain_dir/.manifest.repair.XXXXXX")"

jq 'del(.sources.seed.history_coverage.checkpointed_unexported_commits)' \
  "$brain_dir/manifest.json" > "$brain_manifest_tmp"

jq -e '
  (.schema_version == 3) and
  (.sources.seed.history_coverage
    | has("checkpointed_unexported_commits")
    | not)
' "$brain_manifest_tmp" >/dev/null

chmod 600 "$brain_manifest_tmp"
mv "$brain_manifest_tmp" "$brain_dir/manifest.json"
```

Confirm that the manifest now parses:

```sh
entire brain status --json | jq '.brain, .issues'
```

`manifest_state` should now be `current`. An FTS migration warning is expected at this point.

## 5. Migrate the old derived indexes

Preview first:

```sh
entire brain memory migrate --dry-run --json
```

Then perform the migration:

```sh
entire brain memory migrate --json
```

If it is interrupted, resume with:

```sh
entire brain memory migrate --resume --json
```

If any command still reports `memory_state_corrupt`, stop there and preserve the backups—do not reset the Brain.

## 6. Perform the full deterministic refresh

```sh
entire brain refresh --agent none --force
```

This performs the complete sequence:

1. Export retained Entire sessions.
2. Refresh deterministic seed context.
3. Rebuild history and conversation projections.
4. Rebuild document indexes.
5. Generate a fresh committed-state Graph snapshot.
6. Reconcile existing facts.
7. Rebuild the pattern layer.
8. Print final status.

`--agent none` means no hosted-model calls or token spending. Given the repository size—about 2,640 exported sessions and 5.3 GB of session data—expect this step to take a while.

## 7. Verify the initialized Brain

```sh
entire brain status --json --details
entire brain doctor --json
entire brain memory status --json
entire brain memory repair --dry-run --json
entire brain stats --json
entire plugin doctor
```

Check that:

- `manifest_state` is `current`.
- Seed, sessions, history, docs, facts, and semantic sources are present.
- The semantic commit matches:

```sh
git rev-parse HEAD
```

- There are no `memory_state_corrupt` or `memory_migration_required` findings.
- The repair dry-run does not request another rebuild.

Then smoke-test retrieval:

```sh
entire brain overview
entire brain brief "explain the architecture and likely test commands" --json
entire brain search "checkpoint" --json
```

## 8. Build the new entity-history index

This enables questions such as “which checkpoints changed this function?”

For a bounded first pass:

```sh
entire brain entities backfill --json
```

For complete first-parent history:

```sh
entire brain entities backfill --limit 0 --json
```

The complete pass may be lengthy on this repository. Once built, deterministic refreshes keep its tip current.

## 9. Restore the temporarily stashed files

If you used the stash:

```sh
cd ~/Projects/entire.io
git stash pop
git status --short
```

Those untracked files will not be part of the committed-state Brain. If they should be indexed, commit them and rerun the normal refresh. To deliberately index an uncommitted worktree, use the required two-step path:

```sh
entire brain refresh --agent none --worktree
entire brain refresh index --force --worktree
```

Worktree-backed semantic snapshots cannot be exported as bundles.

## 10. Refresh outdated agent hooks

Codex and Gemini are already current. Update the other installed integrations:

```sh
entire agent add claude-code --force
entire agent add opencode --force
entire agent add pi --force

entire status --detailed
git status --short
```

Review and commit any intentional repository configuration changes.

## 11. Connect Brain to Codex through MCP

Merge this into the existing `~/Projects/entire.io/.codex/config.toml`; do not remove its current Chrome DevTools entry:

```toml
[mcp_servers.entire_brain]
command = "entire"
args = ["brain", "mcp"]
cwd = "/Users/thomi/Projects/entire.io"
```

Codex supports project-scoped MCP servers in trusted `.codex/config.toml` files and defines local stdio servers using `[mcp_servers.<name>]`, `command`, `args`, and optional `cwd`. [Official OpenAI Codex MCP documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli)

Restart Codex, then verify with `/mcp` or:

```sh
codex mcp list
```

For clients that consume `.mcp.json`, merge this server alongside the existing entries:

```json
"entire-brain": {
  "command": "entire",
  "args": ["brain", "mcp"]
}
```

## 12. Keep it fresh

Run the deterministic watcher in a dedicated terminal:

```sh
cd ~/Projects/entire.io
entire brain watch
```

Optional fact distillation spends tokens and should begin with an estimate:

```sh
entire brain distill --dry-run --json
entire brain distill --agent codex --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low
entire brain facts status --json
```

The core initialization workflow is also documented in [getting-started.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/docs/getting-started.md:117).

```sh
cd ~/Projects/entire.io

  [[ -n "$brain_dir" ]] || {
    echo "error: entire brain path returned an empty path" >&2
    exit 1
  }

  [[ -f "$brain_dir/manifest.json" ]] || {
    echo "error: manifest not found at $brain_dir/manifest.json" >&2
    exit 1
  }

  echo "Repairing: $brain_dir/manifest.json"

  brain_manifest_tmp="$(mktemp "${brain_dir}/.manifest.repair.XXXXXX")"

  jq 'del(.sources.seed.history_coverage.checkpointed_unexported_commits)' \
    "$brain_dir/manifest.json" > "$brain_manifest_tmp"

  jq -e '
    (.schema_version == 3) and
    (.sources.seed.history_coverage
      | has("checkpointed_unexported_commits")
      | not)

  echo "Manifest repaired successfully."
)
```

```sh
entire brain status --json | jq '.brain, .issues'
```

1. Enable base Entire capture in the existing repository. Brain assumes the Entire CLI, repository enablement, and target-agent hooks already exist ([README.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/README.md:51)). Exact host commands:

```sh
cd /path/to/repo
entire enable --agent codex       # or claude-code, gemini, cursor, etc.
entire agent add <other-agent>    # optional additional integrations
entire status
entire agent list
```

`entire enable` creates settings, installs Git hooks, and installs the selected agent hooks; interactive `entire enable` prompts for agents ([Entire CLI README](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-cli/README.md:131), [agent_group.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go:16)). Check `git status` afterward because these repository configuration files may need committing or stashing before semantic indexing.

2. Install Graph and Brain. Current-head source installation requires Entire, Git, Go 1.26, and a cgo-capable toolchain for Graph ([README.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/README.md:53)):

```sh
cd /path/to/sources
git clone --branch main https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph.git
git clone --branch main https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain.git
cd entire-brain
scripts/install.sh
```

For a non-sibling Graph checkout:

```sh
ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR=/path/to/entire-graph scripts/install.sh
```

The script installs Graph, installs Brain, runs `entire brain config init`, then `entire brain doctor` ([scripts/install.sh](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/scripts/install.sh:14)). The plugin manifest formally declares `graph` as Brain’s dependency ([entire-plugin.yml](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/entire-plugin.yml:1)).

3. Verify installation and provider:

```sh
entire graph version
entire graph doctor --json
entire brain version
entire brain config path
entire brain config show
entire brain doctor --json
entire plugin doctor
```

Graph doctor must report `no_egress`, `no_egress_verified`, or `local_only`; Brain refuses semantic indexing if that cannot be verified ([semantic.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/semantic.go:940)). `brain doctor --json` checks plugin directories and, when run in the repository, the capture→export→index→recall chain ([doctor.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/doctor.go:22)).

Brain’s `brain.json` is plugin-global, not repository-specific, and contains only `greeting` plus persisted custom-host `domain_slugs` ([config.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/config/config.go:12)). On an upgrade, inspect/preserve it before running the end-to-end installer: `config init` writes defaults through `Save` and does not perform an existence check ([internal/cli/config.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/config.go:52), [internal/config/config.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/config/config.go:66)). Missing config otherwise loads defaults automatically.

4. If this repository already has an older local Brain, inspect and migrate derived state before refreshing:

```sh
cd /path/to/repo
entire brain doctor --json
entire brain memory status --json
entire brain memory migrate --dry-run --json
entire brain memory migrate --json
# Only after an interrupted migration:
entire brain memory migrate --resume --json
```

Run migration only when status reports findings. It upgrades derived schemas beside the old state and switches atomically; newer unsupported schemas remain read-only and require a newer binary ([semantic_mcp_guide.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/docs/semantic_mcp_guide.md:169), [memory_admin.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/memory_admin.go:862)).

```sh
entire brain status --json --details
```


```sh

entire brain refresh index --worktree
```

```sh

```

Standalone `refresh index` otherwise refuses to replace an existing index ([semantic.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/semantic.go:415)). Worktree-backed semantic indexes cannot be bundle-exported. Also note that an ordinary dirty refresh discovers the dirtiness late, after earlier refresh stages may already have written derived state, so checking cleanliness first matters.


Register that exact command as the agent client’s local stdio MCP server, launched with the target repository as its working directory. item.stdout:
entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, seed
context, docs, history, semantic records, and durable facts, then exposes
retrieval, verification, evaluation, and MCP surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Create the brain:
  add              Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  distill          Distill captured sessions into durable facts (agent-required)
  path             Print the persistent brain path for a repo path or URL
  patterns         Inspect and rebuild repeated-work patterns derived from session history
  refresh          Create or refresh the repository brain
  remember         Author a durable fact about this repository
  status           Summarize the brain: sources, facts, semantic coverage/freshness/blind spots, and live workspace state
  watch            Keep the brain fresh automatically (deterministic refresh is free; agent steps are gated)
  workspace        Manage local multi-repo brain workspaces

Explore the brain:
  brief            Build a bounded task packet from brain context and live state
  dash             Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard (status, facts, sessions, history, semantic)
  entities         Query the persisted entity -> checkpoint index (which checkpoints changed a symbol)
  get              Fetch one item in full by id (fact:… | review:… | history:… | conversation:… | conversation-session:… | doc:… | pattern:… | theme:…)
  guide            Print the recommended coding-agent brain command set
  inspect          Run specialist brain inspection commands
  mcp              Serve local brain tools over MCP stdio
  multi-get        Fetch multiple items by id
  overview         Summarize what the project is: stack, boundaries, commands, and recent decisions
  query            Hybrid (lexical+vector, RRF) search across the brain
  recall           Retrieve durable facts matching a query for the current branch
  search           Lexical keyword search across facts, history, and docs (BM25 for history and docs; token-overlap for facts)
  show             Show one semantic brain record
  verify           Verify durable fact anchors against local retained sources
  viz              Explore the brain as a visual graph in your browser (local, offline)
  vsearch          Vector (semantic) search across facts and docs (history and conversation join with a Gemma-class embedder on the brain_cgo build)

Maintain & share:
  bench            Run local benchmark helpers
  bundle           Import or export local brain bundles
  facts            Review, promote, and garbage-collect durable facts
  gc               Prune old local semantic overlays and snapshots
  help             Help about any command
  memory           Inspect and drive the durable conversation-projection work record (hints, jobs, receipts)
  privacy          List, exclude, include, and purge captured sessions from the brain's projections
  publish          Publish the local brain to hosted Entire (opt-in)
  repair           Rebuild local semantic brain derived indexes
  reset            Remove local generated brain data
  stats            Report brain counts and ranges by branch, agent, source, completion state, and index version
  version          Print plugin version

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for entire-brain

Use "entire-brain [command] --help" for more information about a command.

  search           Lexical keyword search across facts, history, and docs (BM25 for history and docs; token-overlap for facts)

  viz              Explore the brain as a visual graph in your browser (local, offline)

  repair           Rebuild local semantic brain derived indexes

At HEAD `58b0c54e`, this is expected lazy-cache behavior, not source corruption.

Why the commands disagree:

- A full refresh publishes a new canonical history projection, but explicitly leaves FTS lazy: the old fingerprint makes it unusable until the next query rebuilds it ([history.go:539](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history.go:539)).
- Read-only status sees FTS schema `1` versus supported schema `3` and reports `memory_migration_required` ([memory_health_schema.go:213](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/memory_health_schema.go:213)).
- `memory migrate` does not include FTS in its migration detector; FTS health and migration findings are separate fields ([memory_admin.go:695](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/memory_admin.go:695), [memory_admin.go:1899](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/memory_admin.go:1899)).
- `memory repair` only considers canonical index integrity, privacy verification, projection receipts, and session fingerprint when deciding `needsRebuild`; FTS is not a trigger ([memory_admin.go:457](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/memory_admin.go:457)).
- There is no dedicated `memory fts rebuild` subcommand ([memory_cmd.go:29](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/memory_cmd.go:29)).

The safest supported repair is simply a lexical history query:

```sh
cd ~/Projects/entire.io
entire brain search "repository architecture" \
  --source history \
  --limit 1 \
  --json >/dev/null
```

`search` is the lexical/BM25 command and supports `--source history` ([retrieve_cmd.go:70](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/retrieve_cmd.go:70), [retrieve_cmd.go:107](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/retrieve_cmd.go:107)). On an old or stale FTS schema, the query loads verified canonical history, takes the Brain write lock, and rebuilds the FTS tables to schema 3 ([history_fts.go:122](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:122), [history_fts.go:180](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:180), [history_fts.go:249](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:249)). It does not delete history, sessions, or facts.

Manual deletion is an explicitly supported fallback: the file is documented as disposable, with deletion forcing reconstruction on the next query ([history_fts.go:17](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:17)). It should not be necessary for a valid schema-1 database—the query can migrate it in place.

```sh

quarantine="$(mktemp -d /tmp/entire-brain-fts.XXXXXX)"

for artifact in "$fts" "${fts}-wal" "${fts}-shm" "${fts}-journal"; do

done

  --source history \
  --limit 1 \
  --json >/dev/null
```

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/fts_rebuild_path
Payload:
The installed pure-Go binary can create schema-v3 FTS5. It fails on this repository’s canonical history data, not because CGO is disabled.

Confirmed cause:

- Current history contains 1,559,212 records.
- A streaming read-only check found duplicate ID `history:6d3e9386b563dc805d7dfb0b` at rows 90,233 and 90,235.
- Both are identical `code_fact` records from the same transcript path and line.
- The history builder only explicitly deduplicates decisions and conversations, so duplicate code-fact IDs survive into `index.json` ([history.go:1301](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history.go:1301)).
- FTS v3 declares `history_records.id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` ([history_fts.go:264](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:264)).

Therefore the exact swallowed error is:


content.text: How to fix the BM25 issue?
How to fix the BM25 issue?

The proper fix belongs in Entire Brain’s history builder—not in `entire.io` data and not in the SQLite configuration.

Root cause: two identical `code_fact` records share ID `history:6d3e9386b563dc805d7dfb0b`. FTS v3 requires unique IDs, so its transaction fails and search silently falls back.

Recommended code fix:

1. In [history.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history.go:1301), deduplicate every history record by stable ID before writing `index.json`.

   - Identical ID and payload: retain the first record.
   - Identical ID but different payload: return an explicit collision error.
   - Preserve deterministic ordering.

2. Keep the unique constraint in [history_fts.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:264). Using `INSERT OR IGNORE` or removing `UNIQUE` would conceal real ID collisions.

3. Harden FTS publication:

   - Build into a temporary SQLite file.
   - Run integrity checks.
   - Rename it into place only after success.
   - Remove the temporary file on failure.
   - Surface the build error instead of silently discarding it at [history_fts.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:807).

4. Add tests for exact duplicate suppression, conflicting ID detection, and failed FTS builds leaving no corrupt stub.

Then rebuild and regenerate:

```sh
cd ~/Projects/entire-brain
go test ./...
scripts/install-local.sh

cd ~/Projects/entire.io
entire brain refresh history

entire brain search "repository architecture" \
  --source history \
  --limit 1 \
  --json >/dev/null

entire brain memory status --json | jq '{fts, issues}'
entire brain doctor --json
```

Expected FTS result:

```json
{
  "present": true,
  "schema_version": "3",
  "state": "current"
}
```

Until that code change lands, leaving FTS absent is the safest state; history search continues through the substring fallback. Editing `history/index.json` manually or reinstalling with CGO will not fix it.

   The repository-consistent remediation is the pinned publication pattern in [pattern_corpus.go:759](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/pattern_corpus.go:759) and [pattern_corpus.go:1044](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/pattern_corpus.go:1044):

   - Pin Brain and `history/` with `os.OpenRoot`/`OpenRoot`.
   - Copy into an `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` descriptor-rooted candidate.
   - Inspect/remove/rename only through `*os.Root`.
   - Use `syncPinnedDirectory`.
   - Use the existing durable-marker protocol if sidecars require a multi-step transition.

[history_fts.go:496](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:496) runs a second full-database `integrity_check` on every stale rebuild.    - successful `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` with no busy frames;
   - exact `PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE` result;
   - successful close;

[history_fts_test.go:557](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts_test.go:557) injects rename failure only against a new DELETE-mode cache.

- Reconciliation precedes record/kind counts at [history.go:1382](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history.go:1382), receipts at [history.go:378](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history.go:378), and all serialized-index digests/fingerprints at [history.go:390](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history.go:390).

- Compatibility search still falls back at [history_fts.go:934](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:934) and [history_fts.go:919](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain/internal/cli/history_fts.go:919).

item.stdout:
entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, seed
context, docs, history, semantic records, and durable facts, then exposes
retrieval, verification, evaluation, and MCP surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Create the brain:
  add              Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain

appears in multiple checkpoints, the copy with the newest checkpoint timestamp
is selected.

  -o, --output string          Output directory for the export (default: plugin data brain directory)
      --raw                    Export raw agent transcripts instead of normalized compact transcripts
      --scope string           Checkpoint discovery scope: all or branch (default "all")

item.stdout:
Keep the brain fresh automatically (deterministic refresh is free; agent steps are gated)

Usage:
  entire-brain watch [path] [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string                 Agent for the distill step (used only with --distill) (default "codex")
      --budget int                   Cap on gated agent runs this process (distill + seed; each spends tokens); 0 = unlimited. Counts reset on restart — the durable guard against re-spend is --distill-every + the cursor.
      --consolidate-every duration   Minimum interval between full consolidations (heavy refresh); the per-tick short-term delta covers freshness in between. 0 = consolidate on every change; a full short-term buffer always consolidates (default 30m0s)
      --distill                      Run distill (SPENDS TOKENS) when new sessions land — gated by --distill-every + --budget
      --distill-every duration       Minimum interval between gated agent runs (distill and/or seed synthesis) (default 24h0m0s)
      --effort string                Reasoning effort for the gated agent steps (codex --config model_reasoning_effort=, claude --effort)
  -h, --help                         help for watch
      --interval duration            Poll interval between ticks (default 5m0s)
      --jobs int                     Parallel distill extraction jobs when --distill is enabled; reconciliation and writes remain deterministic (default 1)
      --model string                 Fast/cheap model for the gated agent steps (distill/seed)
      --once                         Run a single pass and exit (no daemon loop)
      --seed-agent string            Agent for gated seed synthesis (SPENDS TOKENS); none = deterministic seed only. Bounded by --distill-every + --budget, NOT per-change (default "none")

item.stdout:
delta is the short-term memory path: it incrementally exports session
transcripts from checkpoints (reusing the export cursor), then scans ONLY the
transcripts that changed since the last full index build into a small overlay
(history/short-term.json) that retrieval searches alongside the long-term
index. Seconds even on very large brains.

The next full 'refresh' (or 'refresh history') is consolidation: it absorbs
everything the overlay covers into long-term memory and clears the overlay.
'watch' runs delta on every tick, so an in-flight session's earlier turns are
recallable near-real-time.

Usage:
  entire-brain refresh delta [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help        help for delta
      --no-export   Skip the incremental session export; only re-index already-exported transcripts

  entire-brain watch [path] [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string                 Agent for the distill step (used only with --distill) (default "codex")
      --budget int                   Cap on gated agent runs this process (distill + seed; each spends tokens); 0 = unlimited. Counts reset on restart — the durable guard against re-spend is --distill-every + the cursor.
      --consolidate-every duration   Minimum interval between full consolidations (heavy refresh); the per-tick short-term delta covers freshness in between. 0 = consolidate on every change; a full short-term buffer always consolidates (default 30m0s)
      --distill                      Run distill (SPENDS TOKENS) when new sessions land — gated by --distill-every + --budget
      --distill-every duration       Minimum interval between gated agent runs (distill and/or seed synthesis) (default 24h0m0s)
      --effort string                Reasoning effort for the gated agent steps (codex --config model_reasoning_effort=, claude --effort)
  -h, --help                         help for watch
      --interval duration            Poll interval between ticks (default 5m0s)
      --jobs int                     Parallel distill extraction jobs when --distill is enabled; reconciliation and writes remain deterministic (default 1)
      --model string                 Fast/cheap model for the gated agent steps (distill/seed)
      --once                         Run a single pass and exit (no daemon loop)
      --seed-agent string            Agent for gated seed synthesis (SPENDS TOKENS); none = deterministic seed only. Bounded by --distill-every + --budget, NOT per-change (default "none")

{"i":1,"chunk_id":"a30fc5","wall_time_seconds":0.00000225,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":197,"output":"delta is the short-term memory path: it incrementally exports session
transcripts from checkpoints (reusing the export cursor), then scans ONLY the
transcripts that changed since the last full index build into a small overlay
(history/short-term.json) that retrieval searches alongside the long-term
index. Seconds even on very large brains.

The next full 'refresh' (or 'refresh history') is consolidation: it absorbs
everything the overlay covers into long-term memory and clears the overlay.
'watch' runs delta on every tick, so an in-flight session's earlier turns are
recallable near-real-time.

Usage:
  entire-brain refresh delta [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help        help for delta
      --no-export   Skip the incremental session export; only re-index already-exported transcripts
"}

content.text: The installed CLI has a dedicated `watch` mode. Its default path is token-free: every five minutes it exports only new/changed sessions into a short-term overlay, then consolidates that overlay into long-term memory at most every 30 minutes. I’m checking how it treats source/doc changes and dirty worktrees so the recommended routine covers both conversation memory and code freshness.

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/brain_refresh_cli
Payload:
Authoritative workflow for an existing Brain:

```sh
cd /path/to/repo
entire brain status --json
entire brain refresh --agent none
entire brain status --json
entire brain doctor --json
```

`--agent none` prevents seed synthesis from invoking Codex/Claude. Plain `refresh` defaults to `--agent auto`, which may call an installed agent if the seed needs rebuilding. A successful persistent refresh already prints status afterward.

Clean vs dirty worktrees:

- On a clean tree, `refresh --agent none` is the normal all-layer update.
- Default refresh refuses dirty content when seed or semantic rebuilding is needed:
  - seed: `dirty_worktree: refusing to seed ... without --worktree`
  - semantic: `dirty_worktree: refusing to index ... without --worktree`
- Actual current behavior differs from README prose: `refresh --worktree` refreshes seed/docs from the worktree and intentionally skips the implicit semantic step. This is locked by `TestRefreshWorktreeSkipsImplicitSemanticRebuild`.
- Therefore, to update both layers to the same dirty snapshot, use:

```sh
entire brain refresh --agent none --worktree
entire brain refresh index --force --worktree
entire brain status --json
```

- For semantic only:

```sh
entire brain refresh index --force              # clean HEAD
entire brain refresh index --force --worktree   # intentional dirty snapshot
```

`--force` is required for standalone `refresh index` whenever an index already exists; otherwise it errors with “semantic index already exists; use --force to replace it.” There is no `refresh semantic` command; semantic refresh is `refresh index`. The hidden `--semantic-worktree` full-refresh compatibility flag exists but is deprecated in favor of explicit `refresh index --worktree`. Worktree-backed semantic indexes cannot be bundle-exported.

Layer-specific commands:

```sh
entire brain refresh sessions
entire brain refresh history [path]
entire brain refresh delta
entire brain refresh index [path] --force
entire brain refresh seed [path] --update
entire brain patterns refresh [path] [--json]
entire brain patterns status [path] [--json]
```

Semantics:

- `refresh sessions`: exports the latest transcript per session; persistent exports reuse unchanged transcript files via the export cursor. `--history-index` optionally rebuilds history too.
- `refresh history`: uses already-exported transcripts; it does not export sessions. It rebuilds the logical long-term projection, but per-transcript parsing is digest-cached. It absorbs and clears a matching short-term overlay.
- `refresh delta`: the explicitly incremental fast path—exports incrementally, scans only transcripts differing from long-term history, and writes a retrieval-visible short-term overlay. `--no-export` indexes already-exported changes only.
- `refresh index`: semantic only; no seed/docs/history/pattern rebuild. When triggered, Brain replaces the semantic snapshot/generation rather than applying a Brain-level delta.
- `patterns refresh`: explicit full deterministic rebuild from already-exported sessions; it is token-free. Full `refresh` automatically skips the episode projection when its sessions fingerprint is current and rebuilds it after session changes or `--force`.

Overall incrementality:

- Full `refresh` is freshness-aware, not uniformly incremental:
  - session transcripts are cursor-reused;
  - seed skips when HEAD/snapshot mode is current;
  - history skips entirely when fingerprints/artifacts are current and otherwise reuses per-file parse cache;
  - semantic skips when the clean HEAD tree and artifacts are current, otherwise replaces the snapshot;
  - pattern episodes skip when the sessions fingerprint is current.
- `--force` defeats those freshness skips and forces seed/history/semantic/pattern rebuilding.
- For active repositories, `watch` is the intended automatic workflow: per-tick `refresh delta`, with full consolidation throttled by `--consolidate-every` (default 30m).

Health commands:

- `status [path] [--json] [--details] [--fail-on ...]` reports source presence, semantic and retrieval freshness, blind spots, facts, and live branch/dirty state. Gate choices are `release`, `unsafe`, `degraded`, `blind-spots`, `none`; the report is emitted before a gate returns nonzero.
- `doctor [--json]` is hidden from root help but callable. It is read-only and checks plugin directories plus the capture → export → history/conversation/FTS/memory chain and semantic severity. It reports warn/error states but does not repair them or use those states as a CI failure gate; use `status --fail-on ...` for gating.

- Optional daily fact maintenance:

  ```sh

    --model gpt-5.4-mini --effort low --budget 1
  ```

  Distillation is opt-in, token-spending, and potentially network-egressing. `--budget` resets on restart, while the durable cursor prevents spending again before `--distill-every`.

- Trigger behavior:

  - Every tick: incremental checkpoint export and changed-transcript overlay.
  - Full refresh fingerprint: `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1`, `refs/remotes/origin/entire/checkpoints/v1`, and `HEAD`.
  - Commits/checkouts changing `HEAD` trigger consolidation.
  - Dirty source edits do not trigger or enter semantic indexing.
  - A branch switch at the same commit does not change the fingerprint.
  - New v2 checkpoint refs are ingested by the per-tick delta path, but are not in the full-refresh fingerprint.

- Dirty-worktree caveat: full watch consolidation invokes semantic indexing without `--worktree`, so it can fail with `dirty_worktree`; delta recall remains available until the repository is clean.

- Entire’s normal Git/agent hooks capture sessions and checkpoints only. Brain’s hidden hooks are not installed by `entire enable`. A host must explicitly invoke:

  ```sh
  entire brain hook session-end --session <id> \
    --branch <branch> --agent auto --model <cheap-model> --effort low
  ```

- There is an ephemeral background history worker: lifecycle `memory notify` events and MCP startup can launch `memory worker --once`. It refreshes delta/history projections and retries bounded failures, but does not keep seed/docs/semantic source state current.

- No built-in daemon installer exists. `watch` remains foreground; use `--once` under launchd/cron/systemd, or supervise the continuous command externally.

import {
  http,
  HttpResponse,
  type DefaultBodyType,
  type HttpHandler,
  type HttpResponseInit,
  type RequestHandlerOptions,
} from "msw"

import type { paths } from "./gen/openapi"

type HttpMethod = "get" | "put" | "post" | "delete" | "patch"
type MaybePromise<Value> = Value | Promise<Value>
type Values<ObjectType> = ObjectType[keyof ObjectType]

type PathsForMethod<Method extends HttpMethod> = {
  [Path in keyof paths]: Method extends keyof paths[Path]
    ? [NonNullable<paths[Path][Method]>] extends [never]
      ? never
      : Path
    : never
}[keyof paths]

type OperationFor<
  Method extends HttpMethod,
  Path extends PathsForMethod<Method>,
> = Method extends keyof paths[Path] ? NonNullable<paths[Path][Method]> : never

type ResponsesFor<Method extends HttpMethod, Path extends PathsForMethod<Method>> =
  OperationFor<Method, Path> extends { responses: infer Responses } ? Responses : never

type ResponseContentFor<

looksMinified.

sem: flag minified files only when overlong lines dominate

The old heuristic flagged E_MINIFIED whenever any single line exceeded
5000 bytes. That misclassifies real source containing a few enormous
one-line data literals: microsoft/TypeScript's src/compiler/scanner.ts
(~3,500 ordinary lines plus three >5KB unicode range tables, 11% of its
bytes on overlong lines) was skipped entirely, losing createScanner and
131 other symbols.

New rule: a file is minified/bundled only when bytes on overlong lines
(>5000 bytes) make up >= 70% of the file. Calibrated on the TypeScript
repo's 13 previously flagged files: real-source shapes measure <= 25%
overlong bytes and now parse (scanner.ts probe: 132 symbols including
createScanner), while genuinely line-dominated files (one-line 46KB
comment fixtures, ~1MB single-line literals, webpack-style bundles)
measure >= 86% and stay flagged (6 of the 13, all deliberate test
fixtures under tests/).

Regression tests cover the three shapes: giant-data-lines-in-real-source
(not flagged, symbols extracted), single-line ~500KB bundle (flagged),
and a few-lines-all-overlong bundle (flagged), plus a unit table for
looksMinified.

    Bound two relation-generation blow-ups: SIMILAR_TO buckets + minified files
    
    Two O(n^2)/dense-graph sources that made full-profile snapshots explode in time and
    output on large or asset-heavy repos:
    
    1. SIMILAR_TO did all-pairs within each LSH band bucket; a bucket of k
       mass-duplicated bodies (boilerplate, generated getters) cost O(k^2). Cap bucket
       size (maxBucketMembers=64) and skip oversized ones — those pairs are redundant
       clone-cluster noise and the dominant cost on big repos. Genuine small clone
       groups are unaffected.
    2. Minified/bundled files (e.g. a site's main.js, *.min.js) pack thousands of
       single-letter symbols onto one line, forming a near-complete same-file call
       graph (retrofit: a vendored main.js produced 114,989 of 114,989 CALLS). Skip
       files whose longest line exceeds maxMinifiedLineLen=5000; they are not source.
    
    Effect: retrofit full profile timeout(>60s, 24MB+) -> 8s/17MB; CALLS 114,989 -> <3k.
    Clean repos unaffected (cobra: 1s, 0 skipped, CALLS unchanged); sem tests pass;
    scored metrics unaffected (SIMILAR_TO is never scored; clean corpus has no
    minified files).
    
    NOTE: this does NOT fully unblock the giants. A separate, deeper issue remains —
    entire-sem's call resolution is algorithmically slow on medium-large Rust/Kotlin
    repos at every profile (tokio, 787 .rs files, doesn't finish in 5min even at fast;
    vs C/linux 39M LOC in 65s). That needs hot-path profiling of the resolver, tracked
    as follow-up.

    Add SIMILAR_TO near-clone detection (WP8)
    
    Phase D, WP8: detect near-duplicate symbol bodies via MinHash + LSH over
    normalized function/method bodies and emit SIMILAR_TO edges.
    
    - Deterministic MinHash (fixed splitmix64-seeded coefficients), 64 hashes over
      3-gram token shingles of comment/literal-stripped, lowercased bodies; LSH
      banding (16x4) to find candidate pairs; emit when the estimated Jaccard is
      >= 0.82, using the estimate as confidence.
    - Memory-bounded: each symbol's shingle set is reduced to a 64-value signature
      and discarded, so large repos don't accumulate shingle sets.
    - Tiny bodies (< 8 shingles) are suppressed to avoid boilerplate noise; pairs
      are emitted once (lower ID -> higher ID) for stable output.
    
    SIMILAR_TO added to the vocabulary and capabilities (heuristic_relation_types +
    near_clone_detection feature). go-clones fixture + golden and
    TestSimilarToLinksNearDuplicates (copy-paste pair linked, unrelated function
    not). Docs updated.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Task name: /root
Sender: /root/patch_parse_audit
Payload:
Read-only audit complete. The `E_MINIFIED` is a provider false positive, not a malformed patch.

- `.patch` is explicitly classified as `{language: "Patch", inventoryOnly: true}` in `internal/sem/inventory_languages.go:91`. `languageForPath` selects that entry at `internal/sem/parser.go:3065-3088`.
- If allowed to parse, `TreeSitterParser.ParseWithStatus` sees no grammar and calls `fallbackEntities` (`parser.go:153-194`); Patch reaches the default `inventoryEntities` branch (`parser.go:3113-3155`), producing one stable `document` symbol. No unified-diff or embedded-JavaScript parser exists.
- The bug is ordering: `processProviderFile` applies `looksMinified(content)` before `parseWithProfile` at `internal/sem/provider_parallel.go:157-182`, without considering `langSpec.inventoryOnly`.
- `cobe@2.0.1.patch` is 26,157 bytes over 8 lines. Its removed and added lines are 12,938 and 12,982 bytes. Thus 25,920/26,157 bytes, 99.09%, are on lines over 5,000 bytes, exceeding the 70% rule in `internal/sem/similarity.go:172-214`.
- Reproduction against `entire.io` emitted the Patch file record plus `E_MINIFIED`, but no symbol. The repository has five Patch files and only four Patch symbols; this is the missing fifth.
- This contradicts the advertised inventory contract: inventory-only formats provide stable file/document inventory (`docs/language-support.md:3-14`), and Patch is listed in that tier (`docs/language-support.md:160`).

Correct immediate fix: exempt explicit inventory-only formats from the source-minification gate, e.g. gate it with `!langSpec.inventoryOnly` in `processProviderFile`. That is preferable to a Patch-only exception and preserves the minified-source protection for JavaScript/TypeScript. The original safeguard exists to avoid huge symbol inventories and dense call graphs from bundled code; a Patch fallback emits one document symbol, so parsing it is linear and cannot recreate that explosion.

Do not:

- add this path to `.graphignore`;
- suppress `E_MINIFIED` in a consumer;
- tune the 5,000-byte/70% thresholds to accommodate this file.

Those approaches hide or weaken the symptom while still violating the Patch inventory contract.

Tests should add a Patch-shaped regression with `-` and `+` lines over 5 KB and assert:

- language `Patch`;
- one `document` symbol;
- no `E_MINIFIED`;
- parsed-file count includes it.

The best location is beside `TestInventoryOnlyLanguagesEmitDocumentSymbols` at `provider_test.go:10632-10665`, or beside the minification integration tests at `provider_test.go:4131-4208`. Keep `TestSingleLineBundleFlaggedMinified` and `TestFewLinesAllLongBundleFlaggedMinified` unchanged to prove real `.js` bundles remain skipped. `TestLooksMinified` at `similarity_test.go:8-28` should remain content-only; the language-aware decision belongs in the provider pipeline.

Semantic diff parsing is a separate feature:

- Parsing diff structure—target files and hunks—would be useful and could emit document-like `patched_file`/`hunk` symbols while Patch remains honestly inventory-only.
- Embedded JS should not be parsed directly from raw `+`/`-` lines. Hunks are incomplete compilation units, removed and added sides would create duplicate/phantom symbols, and line/stable-ID provenance is ambiguous without reconstructing whole before/after files.
- For this particular patch, the embedded file is genuinely minified JavaScript, precisely the material the existing safeguard was designed not to turn into a dense call graph.

So the scoped fix is: restore the promised Patch document symbol by bypassing source-minification policy for explicit inventory-only formats; consider structural diff/hunk parsing later, without treating embedded fragments as live repository code. No files were edited.

Payload:
Entire What Happened:

Tell me why: the blame points here.

The current `E_MINIFIED` results are false positives caused by a language-agnostic file-shape heuristic, not parser failures.

### End-to-end production path

1. [`processProviderFile`]( /Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_parallel.go:48) first checks path/shebang support at lines 60–74.
2. Content is read subject to the default 4 MiB cap ([provider.go:37](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:37), [provider.go:1472](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:1472)). Oversize files become `E_FILE_TOO_LARGE` before minified detection.
3. Language is identified by extension first, then shebang ([provider_parallel.go:129](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_parallel.go:129), [shebang.go:101](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/shebang.go:101)). Thus the barrels are already `TypeScript`, and `.patch` is already inventory-only `Patch` ([inventory_languages.go:91](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/inventory_languages.go:91)).
4. After Go build filtering and file-record construction, the size cap runs at [provider_parallel.go:157](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_parallel.go:157), then `looksMinified` runs unconditionally for every language at line 169.
5. A match emits a file record plus `E_MINIFIED`, marks the file unparsed, emits no symbols, and returns before `parseWithProfile` at line 182.
6. Had parsing occurred, TypeScript would use tree-sitter with a 5-second timeout ([parser.go:244](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/parser.go:244), [parser.go:257](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/parser.go:257)); Patch would take the grammar-less fallback and emit one bounded document symbol ([parser.go:192](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/parser.go:192), [parser.go:3113](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/parser.go:3113)).
7. The reducer counts the file and language but not `ParsedFiles` or symbols ([provider.go:1021](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:1021)). `E_MINIFIED` remains visible in `partial_failures`, though it is excluded from the provider’s failure-count contribution to completeness ([provider.go:17899](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:17899)). Search-agent rendering nevertheless labels any partial failure “degraded” ([search.go:1379](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/search.go:1379)), an adjacent presentation inconsistency.

### Exact heuristic and why all three trigger

[`looksMinified`]( /Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/similarity.go:172) counts bytes on lines strictly longer than 5,000 bytes and returns true when those bytes are at least 70% of total file bytes. It has no minimum file size, language, syntax, filename, generated-code, or executable-code check.

- `api/src/gen/entire-core/index.ts`: 16,925 bytes, four lines. Line 4 is 15,317 bytes, so the ratio is **90.4993%**.
- `frontend/src/gen/api-sdk/index.ts`: 32,813 bytes, four lines. Lines 3–4 are 5,024 and 27,732 bytes, so the ratio is **99.8263%**.
- `patches/cobe@2.0.1.patch`: 26,157 bytes, eight lines. Removed/added minified-JS lines are 12,938 and 12,982 bytes, so the ratio is **99.0939%**.

The barrels are legitimate generated modules containing only two enormous named re-export statements:

```ts
export { ... } from './sdk.gen';
export type { ... } from './types.gen';
```

The patch contains a one-line minified bundle twice because unified diff stores both the removed and added line. The detector sees only byte distribution, not that the surrounding file is a Patch document.

### Original performance rationale and history

- Commit `8f0a1fc` introduced the 5,000-byte longest-line skip. Its measured failure was a vendored `main.js` in Retrofit producing **114,989 of 114,989 CALLS**, with full-profile runtime/output over 60 seconds/24 MB. Skipping it reduced the run to about 8 seconds/17 MB and under 3,000 calls.
- Commit `f8f6fdc` changed “any line >5,000” to the present 70%-of-bytes rule after `microsoft/TypeScript/src/compiler/scanner.ts` was falsely skipped due to three giant Unicode-table literals, losing `createScanner` and 131 other symbols. Calibration found ordinary-source cases at ≤25% and bundle-shaped cases at ≥86%.
- Commit `2d565cc` moved the same ordering/behavior into the parallel per-file worker.
- Tests cover embedded giant data lines, one-line bundles, and few-lines-all-long bundles ([provider_test.go:4152](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_test.go:4152), [similarity_test.go:8](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/similarity_test.go:8)); they do not cover export-only barrels or inventory-only patch files.
- `entire explain --commit` was unavailable because the installed CLI has no `explain` command. The rationale above is commit-message/blame backed, not checkpoint-transcript backed.

### Smallest technically correct fix architecture

Keep the existing detector for executable semantic source, but add narrow positive exemptions rather than weakening its thresholds:

1. **Inventory-only provider exemption:** do not apply `E_MINIFIED` to `langSpec.inventoryOnly`. These files never enter tree-sitter and produce one document symbol under the existing 4 MiB cap. For full-profile correctness and defense in depth, inventory-only files should also skip content-derived call/field/data-flow scans after their `DEFINES` relation; otherwise the generic full-profile loop can interpret patch text as calls despite capabilities saying Patch has no CALLS support.

2. **Strict JS/TS barrel exemption:** for JavaScript/TypeScript only, bypass `E_MINIFIED` when a bounded scanner proves that every non-comment, non-whitespace statement is a re-export:
   - `export { ... } from "literal";`
   - `export type { ... } from "literal";`
   - optionally `export * from "literal";`

   Require complete input coverage—any executable declaration or expression makes the exemption fail. This preserves the bundle guard because an actual minified program cannot satisfy the export-only grammar. Existing re-export machinery and patterns around [provider.go:13437](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:13437) can be reused, but the exemption must validate the entire module, not merely find one matching export.

Recommended provider decision:

```go
if looksMinified(content) &&
    !langSpec.inventoryOnly &&
    !isJavaScriptReexportOnlyModule(path, content) {
    // E_MINIFIED
}
```

Add exact regressions for both real generated barrels, an overlong `.patch` that must emit its Patch document symbol, and an adversarial bundle beginning with an export that must remain `E_MINIFIED`. Do not raise 5,000/70%, exempt generated directories, exempt all short-line-count files, or move detection wholesale after parsing; those options reopen the original dense-call-graph/parse-cost failure.

Tell me why: the blame points here.

The current `E_MINIFIED` results are false positives caused by a language-agnostic file-shape heuristic, not parser failures.

### End-to-end production path

1. [`processProviderFile`]( /Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_parallel.go:48) first checks path/shebang support at lines 60–74.
2. Content is read subject to the default 4 MiB cap ([provider.go:37](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:37), [provider.go:1472](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:1472)). Oversize files become `E_FILE_TOO_LARGE` before minified detection.
3. Language is identified by extension first, then shebang ([provider_parallel.go:129](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_parallel.go:129), [shebang.go:101](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/shebang.go:101)). Thus the barrels are already `TypeScript`, and `.patch` is already inventory-only `Patch` ([inventory_languages.go:91](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/inventory_languages.go:91)).
4. After Go build filtering and file-record construction, the size cap runs at [provider_parallel.go:157](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_parallel.go:157), then `looksMinified` runs unconditionally for every language at line 169.

content.text:
You’re right—ignoring them would conceal Graph defects. Brain itself doesn’t parse source; it consumes Entire Graph’s snapshot.

| Files | Actual cause |
|---|---|
| Generated TypeScript barrels | Rejected before parsing by a language-agnostic “minified” heuristic |
| `cobe@2.0.1.patch` | Same heuristic incorrectly runs on an inventory-only format |
| `packages/mocks/src/msw.ts` | Graph’s TypeScript compatibility preprocessing corrupts valid syntax |

The minification check in [provider_parallel.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_parallel.go:169) rejects a file when at least 70% of its bytes occur on lines longer than 5,000 bytes, as implemented in [similarity.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/similarity.go:195). It runs before any parser and has no awareness of language or syntax.

That misclassifies the two valid generated barrels because their long lines are enormous `export { … }` and `export type { … }` declarations:

- API barrel: 90.50% of bytes on overlong lines
- Frontend barrel: 99.83%
- Cobe patch: 99.09%, because the diff contains both old and new one-line minified JavaScript

The heuristic exists for a legitimate reason: a real minified bundle previously produced 114,989 call relations and took over a minute. Its classification is simply too blunt.

The patch bug is especially clear: `.patch` is explicitly declared inventory-only in [inventory_languages.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/inventory_languages.go:91). It should produce one bounded document symbol, but the minification gate returns first. Graph currently has no structural unified-diff parser, so parsing embedded before/after JavaScript would be a separate feature.

`msw.ts` is different. The pinned TypeScript parser parses the original file successfully. Before parsing, however, Graph always applies [maskTypeScriptUnsupportedSyntax](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/parser.go:508). That workaround blanks the generic call-signature header through `): {`, accidentally removing the opening brace while retaining the returned object and its closing brace. The parser then reports the resulting extra `}` at line 120.

The proper repairs are:

1. Exempt inventory-only formats from the minification gate.
2. Recognize strictly re-export-only JS/TS modules before labeling them minified, while retaining protection for executable bundles.
3. Parse TypeScript unmodified first; apply the compatibility mask only when raw parsing fails.
4. Align Brain’s completeness classification with Graph’s intentional-skip semantics. That fixes the misleading status, but does not replace the parsing fixes.

No `.brainignore` entries should be added for these files.

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/typescript_grammar_audit
Payload:
Root cause: Entire Graph’s TypeScript pre-parse mask, not the raw grammar.

- The valid construct is the generic call signature returning an inline object type at `packages/mocks/src/msw.ts:101–119`:

  ```ts
  <Status extends keyof ResponsesFor<Method, Path>>(
    status: Status,
  ): {
    // members
  }
  ```

- Raw pinned tree-sitter parses the complete file and a minimal reproduction with `HasError == false`.
- `maskTypeScriptUnsupportedSyntax` blanks lines 101–103, including the returned object’s opening `{`, then stops masking. Line 119 consequently closes `OpenApiResponse`, making line 120 an extra `}`—exactly the provider’s reported error.
- The mask cannot simply be deleted: pinned tree-sitter still rejects adjacent generic callable overloads, as covered by existing `TakePattern` regressions.

Version evidence:

- `go.mod` pins `github.com/smacker/go-tree-sitter` at `dd81d9e9be82`, dated 2024-08-27.
- Its grammar manifest pins `tree-sitter-typescript` v0.21.2, revision `9f804be960f289a0acc59d8564acc16857b0b088`, ABI 14.
- This roughly two-year-old pinned grammar already supports the exact `msw.ts` syntax. A latest-upstream checkout was unavailable under the no-network constraint, but an upgrade is not required for this failure.

Recommended durable fix:

1. Parse `.ts` source unmodified first.
2. Only if that tree contains errors, retry using `maskTypeScriptUnsupportedSyntax`.
3. Preserve current masked fallback behavior for genuinely unsupported shapes.
4. Apply the same raw-first selection in `js_scopes.go`, which also masks `.ts` unconditionally.

Regression test: add the minimal generic callable returning `{ json: …; empty: … }`, followed by a normal function/dotted call. Assert no `ParseStatus` error, the following entity survives, and scope/call extraction still sees the following call.

Both repositories remain clean; no files were edited.

- [provider_parallel.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_parallel.go:169): ~8–12 production lines.
  - Replace the raw `looksMinified(content)` check with a helper that exempts `langSpec.inventoryOnly` and proven JS/TS re-export-only modules.
- [typescript.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/typescript.go:1): ~35–50 lines.
  - Add a conservative scanner accepting only blank/full-line comments and complete single-line statements of:
    - `export { identifiers... } from "literal";`
    - `export type { identifiers... } from "literal";`
    - `export * [as name] from "literal";`
  - Validate every list item as an identifier or `identifier as identifier`; require complete input coverage. This avoids parsing hostile minified input merely to decide whether parsing is safe.
- [provider.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:3006): one strongly recommended line.
  - Skip content-derived per-symbol scans when `InventoryOnlyLanguage(file.Language)` is true. `DEFINES` has already been emitted. This prevents a newly admitted Patch document from being lexically misread as CALLS in the full profile and reinforces the inventory-only contract.
- [provider_test.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_test.go:4131): ~35–50 test lines.
  - Generate long barrel lines programmatically.
  - Assert both barrel and long Patch files have no `E_MINIFIED`, count as parsed, and Patch emits its document symbol.
  - Assert Patch text containing `someFunction()` does not emit CALLS.
  - Keep the existing real-bundle tests unchanged.
- [typescript_test.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/typescript_test.go:1): ~20–35 lines.
  - Table-test valid named/type/star barrels and reject mixed executable code, malformed entries, comment-only content, and a bundle prefixed by one valid export.

No change is needed in [similarity.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/similarity.go:172) or `TestLooksMinified`: those should continue reporting the three files as line-dominated. The provider policy decides whether that shape is unsafe for the identified language.

Smaller staged alternatives:

1. **Patch-only stage:** inventory bypass plus the full-profile inventory scan gate: ~2 production lines and 20–30 test lines. Fixes cobe safely.
2. **Exact-barrel stage:** single-line strict classifier as above: another ~60–85 production/test lines. This fixes both current generated barrels without claiming multiline support.
3. **General multiline barrels:** a real bounded statement lexer adds roughly 25–40 more production lines and 15–25 tests. It is unnecessary for the current four-line fixtures.

A one-line inventory bypass without the relation-scan gate is the absolute minimum, but it leaves full-profile Patch documents eligible for bogus semantic CALLS. Generator-comment exemptions, directory exemptions, threshold increases, and short-file exemptions are smaller but not technically sound.

Payload:
Estimated diff:

| Area | Functions | Net LOC |
|---|---|---:|
| `internal/sem/parser.go` | `ParseWithStatus`; new shared `parseTreeWithFallback` helper | ~20–30 |
| `internal/sem/js_scopes.go` | `newJSScanState`, `newJSScanStateForContent`, `jsScanGrammar`, `buildJSScanState` | ~15–25 |
| Parser regression | Minimal `msw.ts` callable-object return case | ~25–35 |
| Optional scope regression | Raw/fallback selection or namespace-call case | ~20–25 |

Total: approximately 65–110 LOC across 3–4 files; production code alone about 35–50 LOC.

Recommended implementation shape:

- Supply the parser with raw TypeScript as the primary source and a masked source as an optional fallback.
- A shared helper parses raw once and returns it when the root is valid and error-free.
- If raw has syntax errors and the masked bytes differ, explicitly close the raw native tree and parse masked under the same context/deadline.
- Return the selected source alongside the tree so `jsScopeWalker.src` matches the chosen tree.
- For raw-error cases, retain today’s behavior by choosing the masked result even if it also contains recoverable errors.

Tests:

- Add the exact generic-callable/inline-object-return fixture and a following function; assert no parse error and both symbols survive.
- Existing `TestTreeSitterParserTypeScriptMasksGenericCallableTypeSignatures` already proves masked fallback remains necessary and operational.
- Optionally add a small scope-path test confirming `newJSScanState` receives raw source for the valid fixture.
- Focused existing mask and namespace tests pass: 3 tests in 0.858s.

Risks are low but specific:

- Native tree leakage if the rejected first tree is not closed.
- Doubling parse work only for files where raw parsing errors and masking changes content.
- Preserve the single 5-second budget; separate deadlines could double worst-case latency.
- A raw parse may consume most of the shared budget before fallback, although syntax-error recovery is normally fast.
- Valid raw TypeScript may expose richer AST facts than the old always-masked path; that is intentional but could slightly change symbol inventory.
- `jsScopeWalker` must use the selected raw/masked bytes to preserve node-content correctness.

It’s a small-to-medium Entire Graph change: roughly **165–250 net lines including tests**, with only **80–115 lines of production code** across about 6–8 files.

Breakdown:

- Inventory-only/minification fix: ~100–140 lines
  - Skip the minification gate for inventory-only formats.
  - Add a strict export-only JS/TS barrel classifier.
  - Prevent inventory documents from producing bogus call relations.
  - Most of this is regression testing.

- `msw.ts` TypeScript fix: ~65–110 lines
  - Parse raw TypeScript first, then retry with the compatibility mask only on error.
  - Apply the same selection to scope/call extraction.
  - Production portion is only ~35–50 lines.

There are no schema changes, migrations, CLI changes, or parser upgrades. The main risks are tree-sitter resource cleanup and ensuring the barrel exemption cannot admit real minified bundles; both are straightforward to cover with focused tests.

A real structural unified-diff parser would be separate, adding roughly 210–355 lines. Parsing embedded before/after source from patches would be substantially larger and isn’t needed to resolve the degraded status.

func semanticWarningsContainCode(warnings []semanticWarning, code string) bool {
	for _, warning := range warnings {
		if warning.Code == code {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// semanticParseErrorCode marks files where the tree-sitter parse produced error
// nodes but symbols were still extracted (error-tolerant parse). A small number
// of these is expected for any real codebase — newer language syntax the bundled
// grammar version predates — and does not make the indexed facts unsafe to use.
const semanticParseErrorCode = "E_PARSE_ERROR"

// semanticParseErrorTolerance is the fraction of indexed files that may carry
// only benign parse errors before the brain is reported as degraded. Below this
// threshold the completeness axis stays ok; the failures remain recorded in the
// semantic source so they can still be inspected and acted on. Above it, the
// volume is high enough to suspect a grammar/provider problem worth surfacing.
const semanticParseErrorTolerance = 0.10

// semanticCompletenessAxis classifies partial provider failures. Failures that
// are exclusively benign parse errors and stay under the tolerance fraction keep
// the axis ok; anything else (a non-parse failure code, an uncountable file set,
// or too many parse errors) degrades the brain.
func semanticCompletenessAxis(source *semanticSourceManifest) staleAxis {
	failures := len(source.PartialFailures)
	parseErrors := 0
	for _, failure := range source.PartialFailures {
		if failure.Code == semanticParseErrorCode {
			parseErrors++
		}
	}
	if parseErrors == failures && source.Files > 0 {
		fraction := float64(failures) / float64(source.Files)
		if fraction < semanticParseErrorTolerance {
			return staleAxis{State: "ok", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d files had tolerated parse errors", failures, source.Files)}
		}
		return staleAxis{State: "degraded", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d partial failures in %.0f%% of files", failures, fraction*100)}
	}
	return staleAxis{State: "degraded", Detail: strconv.Itoa(failures) + " partial failures"}
}

func aggregateStaleSeverity(axes map[string]staleAxis) string {
	severity := "ok"
	for _, axis := range axes {
		switch axis.State {
		case "missing", "unsafe", "stale", "dirty-stale", "worktree-overlay-stale":
			return "unsafe"
		case "degraded", "dirty-unindexed":
			severity = "degraded"
		}
	}
	return severity
}

package cli

import "testing"

func TestSemanticCompletenessAxisToleratesFewParseErrors(t *testing.T) {
	parseFailures := make([]semanticWarning, 45)
	for i := range parseFailures {
		parseFailures[i] = semanticWarning{Code: semanticParseErrorCode, Severity: "warning", Detail: "tree-sitter syntax error nodes present"}
	}
	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		source    *semanticSourceManifest
		wantState string
	}{
		{
			name:      "few parse errors stay ok",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 1212, PartialFailures: parseFailures},
			wantState: "ok",
		},
		{
			name:      "too many parse errors degrade",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 100, PartialFailures: parseFailures},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
		{
			name: "non-parse failure always degrades",
			source: &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 1212, PartialFailures: []semanticWarning{
				{Code: "E_SYMBOL_EXTRACTION", Severity: "warning"},
			}},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
		{
			name:      "uncountable file set degrades",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 0, PartialFailures: parseFailures[:1]},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := semanticCompletenessAxis(tc.source)
			if got.State != tc.wantState {
				t.Fatalf("state = %q, want %q (detail: %s)", got.State, tc.wantState, got.Detail)
			}
		})
	}
}

func semanticWarningsContainCode(warnings []semanticWarning, code string) bool {
	for _, warning := range warnings {
		if warning.Code == code {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// semanticParseErrorCode marks files where the tree-sitter parse produced error
// nodes but symbols were still extracted (error-tolerant parse). A small number
// of these is expected for any real codebase — newer language syntax the bundled
// grammar version predates — and does not make the indexed facts unsafe to use.
const semanticParseErrorCode = "E_PARSE_ERROR"

// semanticParseErrorTolerance is the fraction of indexed files that may carry
// only benign parse errors before the brain is reported as degraded. Below this
// threshold the completeness axis stays ok; the failures remain recorded in the
// semantic source so they can still be inspected and acted on. Above it, the
// volume is high enough to suspect a grammar/provider problem worth surfacing.
const semanticParseErrorTolerance = 0.10

// semanticCompletenessAxis classifies partial provider failures. Failures that
// are exclusively benign parse errors and stay under the tolerance fraction keep
// the axis ok; anything else (a non-parse failure code, an uncountable file set,
// or too many parse errors) degrades the brain.
func semanticCompletenessAxis(source *semanticSourceManifest) staleAxis {
	failures := len(source.PartialFailures)
	parseErrors := 0
	for _, failure := range source.PartialFailures {
		if failure.Code == semanticParseErrorCode {
			parseErrors++
		}
	}
	if parseErrors == failures && source.Files > 0 {
		fraction := float64(failures) / float64(source.Files)
		if fraction < semanticParseErrorTolerance {
			return staleAxis{State: "ok", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d files had tolerated parse errors", failures, source.Files)}
		}
		return staleAxis{State: "degraded", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d partial failures in %.0f%% of files", failures, fraction*100)}
	}
	return staleAxis{State: "degraded", Detail: strconv.Itoa(failures) + " partial failures"}
}

func aggregateStaleSeverity(axes map[string]staleAxis) string {
	severity := "ok"
	for _, axis := range axes {
		switch axis.State {
		case "missing", "unsafe", "stale", "dirty-stale", "worktree-overlay-stale":
			return "unsafe"
		case "degraded", "dirty-unindexed":
			severity = "degraded"
		}
	}
	return severity
}

	limit   int
	offset  int
	json    bool
	details bool
}

type semanticContextOptions struct {
	limit          int

	includeContent bool
	json           bool

}

type semanticContextResult struct {
	Symbols   []semanticRecord  `json:"symbols"`
	Relations []semanticRecord  `json:"relations"`
	Neighbors []semanticRecord  `json:"neighbors,omitempty"`
	Content   []semanticContent `json:"content,omitempty"`
package cli

import "testing"

func TestSemanticCompletenessAxisToleratesFewParseErrors(t *testing.T) {
	parseFailures := make([]semanticWarning, 45)
	for i := range parseFailures {
		parseFailures[i] = semanticWarning{Code: semanticParseErrorCode, Severity: "warning", Detail: "tree-sitter syntax error nodes present"}
	}
	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		source    *semanticSourceManifest
		wantState string
	}{
		{
			name:      "few parse errors stay ok",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 1212, PartialFailures: parseFailures},
			wantState: "ok",
		},
		{
			name:      "too many parse errors degrade",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 100, PartialFailures: parseFailures},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
		{
			name: "non-parse failure always degrades",
			source: &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 1212, PartialFailures: []semanticWarning{
				{Code: "E_SYMBOL_EXTRACTION", Severity: "warning"},
			}},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
		{
			name:      "uncountable file set degrades",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 0, PartialFailures: parseFailures[:1]},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := semanticCompletenessAxis(tc.source)
			if got.State != tc.wantState {
				t.Fatalf("state = %q, want %q (detail: %s)", got.State, tc.wantState, got.Detail)
			}
		})
	}
}

func semanticWarningsContainCode(warnings []semanticWarning, code string) bool {
	for _, warning := range warnings {
		if warning.Code == code {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// semanticParseErrorCode marks files where the tree-sitter parse produced error
// nodes but symbols were still extracted (error-tolerant parse). A small number
// of these is expected for any real codebase — newer language syntax the bundled
// grammar version predates — and does not make the indexed facts unsafe to use.
const semanticParseErrorCode = "E_PARSE_ERROR"

// semanticParseErrorTolerance is the fraction of indexed files that may carry
// only benign parse errors before the brain is reported as degraded. Below this
// threshold the completeness axis stays ok; the failures remain recorded in the
// semantic source so they can still be inspected and acted on. Above it, the
// volume is high enough to suspect a grammar/provider problem worth surfacing.
const semanticParseErrorTolerance = 0.10

// semanticCompletenessAxis classifies partial provider failures. Failures that
// are exclusively benign parse errors and stay under the tolerance fraction keep
// the axis ok; anything else (a non-parse failure code, an uncountable file set,
// or too many parse errors) degrades the brain.
func semanticCompletenessAxis(source *semanticSourceManifest) staleAxis {
	failures := len(source.PartialFailures)
	parseErrors := 0
	for _, failure := range source.PartialFailures {
		if failure.Code == semanticParseErrorCode {
			parseErrors++
		}
	}
	if parseErrors == failures && source.Files > 0 {
		fraction := float64(failures) / float64(source.Files)
		if fraction < semanticParseErrorTolerance {
			return staleAxis{State: "ok", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d files had tolerated parse errors", failures, source.Files)}
		}
		return staleAxis{State: "degraded", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d partial failures in %.0f%% of files", failures, fraction*100)}
	}
	return staleAxis{State: "degraded", Detail: strconv.Itoa(failures) + " partial failures"}
}

func aggregateStaleSeverity(axes map[string]staleAxis) string {
	severity := "ok"
	for _, axis := range axes {
		switch axis.State {
		case "missing", "unsafe", "stale", "dirty-stale", "worktree-overlay-stale":
			return "unsafe"
		case "degraded", "dirty-unindexed":
			severity = "degraded"
		}
	}
	return severity
}

package cli

import "testing"

func TestSemanticCompletenessAxisToleratesFewParseErrors(t *testing.T) {
	parseFailures := make([]semanticWarning, 45)
	for i := range parseFailures {
		parseFailures[i] = semanticWarning{Code: semanticParseErrorCode, Severity: "warning", Detail: "tree-sitter syntax error nodes present"}
	}
	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		source    *semanticSourceManifest
		wantState string
	}{
		{
			name:      "few parse errors stay ok",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 1212, PartialFailures: parseFailures},
			wantState: "ok",
		},
		{
			name:      "too many parse errors degrade",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 100, PartialFailures: parseFailures},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
		{
			name: "non-parse failure always degrades",
			source: &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 1212, PartialFailures: []semanticWarning{
				{Code: "E_SYMBOL_EXTRACTION", Severity: "warning"},
			}},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
		{
			name:      "uncountable file set degrades",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 0, PartialFailures: parseFailures[:1]},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := semanticCompletenessAxis(tc.source)
			if got.State != tc.wantState {
				t.Fatalf("state = %q, want %q (detail: %s)", got.State, tc.wantState, got.Detail)
			}
		})
	}
}

func semanticWarningsContainCode(warnings []semanticWarning, code string) bool {
	for _, warning := range warnings {
		if warning.Code == code {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// semanticParseErrorCode marks files where the tree-sitter parse produced error
// nodes but symbols were still extracted (error-tolerant parse). A small number
// of these is expected for any real codebase — newer language syntax the bundled
// grammar version predates — and does not make the indexed facts unsafe to use.
const semanticParseErrorCode = "E_PARSE_ERROR"

// semanticParseErrorTolerance is the fraction of indexed files that may carry
// only benign parse errors before the brain is reported as degraded. Below this
// threshold the completeness axis stays ok; the failures remain recorded in the
// semantic source so they can still be inspected and acted on. Above it, the
// volume is high enough to suspect a grammar/provider problem worth surfacing.
const semanticParseErrorTolerance = 0.10

// semanticCompletenessAxis classifies partial provider failures. Failures that
// are exclusively benign parse errors and stay under the tolerance fraction keep
// the axis ok; anything else (a non-parse failure code, an uncountable file set,
// or too many parse errors) degrades the brain.
func semanticCompletenessAxis(source *semanticSourceManifest) staleAxis {
	failures := len(source.PartialFailures)
	parseErrors := 0
	for _, failure := range source.PartialFailures {
		if failure.Code == semanticParseErrorCode {
			parseErrors++
		}
	}
	if parseErrors == failures && source.Files > 0 {
		fraction := float64(failures) / float64(source.Files)
		if fraction < semanticParseErrorTolerance {
			return staleAxis{State: "ok", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d files had tolerated parse errors", failures, source.Files)}
		}
		return staleAxis{State: "degraded", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d partial failures in %.0f%% of files", failures, fraction*100)}
	}
	return staleAxis{State: "degraded", Detail: strconv.Itoa(failures) + " partial failures"}
}

func aggregateStaleSeverity(axes map[string]staleAxis) string {
	severity := "ok"
	for _, axis := range axes {
		switch axis.State {
		case "missing", "unsafe", "stale", "dirty-stale", "worktree-overlay-stale":
			return "unsafe"
		case "degraded", "dirty-unindexed":
			severity = "degraded"
		}
	}
	return severity
}

func TestSemanticCompletenessAxisToleratesFewParseErrors(t *testing.T) {
	parseFailures := make([]semanticWarning, 45)
	for i := range parseFailures {
		parseFailures[i] = semanticWarning{Code: semanticParseErrorCode, Severity: "warning", Detail: "tree-sitter syntax error nodes present"}

	cases := []struct {
		name      string

	}{
		{

			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 1212, PartialFailures: parseFailures},
			wantState: "ok",
		},
		{
			name:      "too many parse errors degrade",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 100, PartialFailures: parseFailures},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
		{
			name: "non-parse failure always degrades",
			source: &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 1212, PartialFailures: []semanticWarning{
				{Code: "E_SYMBOL_EXTRACTION", Severity: "warning"},
			}},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
		{
			name:      "uncountable file set degrades",
			source:    &semanticSourceManifest{Files: 0, PartialFailures: parseFailures[:1]},
			wantState: "degraded",
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := semanticCompletenessAxis(tc.source)
			if got.State != tc.wantState {
				t.Fatalf("state = %q, want %q (detail: %s)", got.State, tc.wantState, got.Detail)
			}
		})
	}
}

entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, seed
context, docs, history, semantic records, and durable facts, then exposes
retrieval, verification, evaluation, and MCP surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Create the brain:
  add              Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  distill          Distill captured sessions into durable facts (agent-required)
  path             Print the persistent brain path for a repo path or URL
  patterns         Inspect and rebuild repeated-work patterns derived from session history
  refresh          Create or refresh the repository brain
  remember         Author a durable fact about this repository
  status           Summarize the brain: sources, facts, semantic coverage/freshness/blind spots, and live workspace state
  watch            Keep the brain fresh automatically (deterministic refresh is free; agent steps are gated)
  workspace        Manage local multi-repo brain workspaces

Explore the brain:
  brief            Build a bounded task packet from brain context and live state
  dash             Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard (status, facts, sessions, history, semantic)
  entities         Query the persisted entity -> checkpoint index (which checkpoints changed a symbol)
  get              Fetch one item in full by id (fact:… | review:… | history:… | conversation:… | conversation-session:… | doc:… | pattern:… | theme:…)
  guide            Print the recommended coding-agent brain command set
  inspect          Run specialist brain inspection commands
  mcp              Serve local brain tools over MCP stdio
  multi-get        Fetch multiple items by id
  overview         Summarize what the project is: stack, boundaries, commands, and recent decisions
  query            Hybrid (lexical+vector, RRF) search across the brain
  recall           Retrieve durable facts matching a query for the current branch
  search           Lexical keyword search across facts, history, and docs (BM25 for history and docs; token-overlap for facts)
  show             Show one semantic brain record
  verify           Verify durable fact anchors against local retained sources
  viz              Explore the brain as a visual graph in your browser (local, offline)
  vsearch          Vector (semantic) search across facts and docs (history and conversation join with a Gemma-class embedder on the brain_cgo build)

Maintain & share:
  bench            Run local benchmark helpers
  bundle           Import or export local brain bundles
  facts            Review, promote, and garbage-collect durable facts
  gc               Prune old local semantic overlays and snapshots
  help             Help about any command
  memory           Inspect and drive the durable conversation-projection work record (hints, jobs, receipts)
  privacy          List, exclude, include, and purge captured sessions from the brain's projections
  publish          Publish the local brain to hosted Entire (opt-in)
  repair           Rebuild local semantic brain derived indexes
  reset            Remove local generated brain data
  stats            Report brain counts and ranges by branch, agent, source, completion state, and index version
  version          Print plugin version

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for entire-brain

Use "entire-brain [command] --help" for more information about a command.
